battle.name: 北周滅北齊之戰
battle.brief: 建德元年冬起，北周二十萬眾圍平陽，拉開歷時五年的滅齊之戰；建德四年斛律光戰歿汾水，齊軍精騎崩散；建德五年正月大軍入鄴，齊後主出奔青州被擒，北齊亡國。卡面羅馬短劍是公元前一世紀的羅馬佩劍，五七二年的中原並無此器，只作對照。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 北周一方：五五七年宇文覺代西魏建周，都長安，疆域以關中為核心，兼有河西走廊、漢中與五五四年新取的益州，與北齊隔河、隔太行相望。軍制承自西魏府兵，柱國與大將軍各領一軍，軍下設師、旅，兵皆編戶，農隙徵發，戰罷歸農。宇文邕五七二年十月在宮中殺死大冢宰宇文護而親政，收相府之權於皇帝，二十四軍分隸中外大都督，又整軍經武、大興屯田，使關中的兵源與馬政重新充實；軍中骨幹是漢人與鮮卑、氐、羯將領結成的關隴集團。北周同時遣使結好北突厥，東與陳朝維持和好，可以專力對齊。北齊一方：五五〇年高洋受魏禪建齊，都鄴，據河北、山東、豫北、晉南與河內，幅員與戶口遠勝北周。軍隊以鮮卑騎兵為精銳，漢人充步卒與攻城之役，漢將與鮮卑將混編一軍；軍令經尚書省與大將軍府下達，前線多以大將軍、柱國為統帥，鄴城另置京畿宿衛與城防之制。但齊廷內部有一道致命裂縫：乳母婁太后與幼主高緯寵信和士開、祖珽等權臣，斛律光、高長恭一輩宿將只握兵柄而不得預政，朝廷內耗直接削弱北齊的戰爭動員能力。柔然控弦漠北而附於北齊，北周則結好突厥，兩翼牽制的消長，是此役外在的關鍵變數。
countriesEn: The Northern Zhou side: in 557 Yuwen Jue replaced the Western Wei and founded the Zhou, with its capital at Chang'an. Its territory had its core in Guanzhong and took in the Hexi corridor, Hanzhong and the Shu region seized in 554; it faced the Northern Qi across the Yellow River and across the Taihang mountains. The army was built on the fubing of the Western Wei: pillar lords and generals each commanded a division, the divisions were subdivided into corps and regiments, and the soldiers were enrolled households called up in the slack farming season and sent back to their fields after the campaign. In the tenth month of 572 Yuwen Yong killed the great chancellor Yuwen Hu inside the palace and took the reins himself, folding the authority of the chancellery back into the emperor, placing the twenty-four divisions under the central command, rebuilding the army, expanding the garrison farms and restoring the manpower and the remounts of Guanzhong. The backbone of that army was the Guanlong group, a military aristocracy welded together out of Han officers and Xianbei, Di and Jie commanders. At the same time the Zhou sent envoys to befriend the Northern Turks and kept peace with the Chen dynasty in the south, so that it could concentrate everything on Qi. The Northern Qi side: in 550 Gao Yang took the abdication of the Wei and founded Qi, with its capital at Ye; it held Hebei, Shandong, northern Henan, southern Shanxi and the Henei region, and in both territory and registered households it was far larger than the Zhou. Its elite was Xianbei cavalry, with Han soldiers filling the infantry and the assault works, Han and Xianbei commanders mixed within the same units. Orders travelled down through the Department of State Affairs and the offices of the great generals, the front was usually commanded by a great general or a pillar lord, and Ye had its own capital garrison and an elaborate system of city defence. But one fatal fissure ran through the Qi court: the wet nurse Lou and the boy emperor Gao Wei favoured powerful ministers such as He Shikai and Zu Ting, while veterans like Hulü Guang and Gao Changgong held the troops without a say in policy; the infighting at court directly crippled Qi's capacity to mobilise for war. The Rouran held the strings of their bows in the northern steppe and attached themselves to Qi, while the Zhou made friends with the Turks; the balance of those two flanking pressures was the decisive external variable of the war.
people: 北周：宇文邕，即北周武帝，五七一年高湛崩後他以幼齡即位，至五七八年崩，在位期間最大的動作是五七二年十月殺大冢宰宇文護而親政，收兵柄於中外大都督，建德四年十月自將諸軍東出，志在滅齊。宇文憲封齊王，為諸軍元帥，主平陽、汾水一路；宇文忻、宇文盛、辛術、豆盧勳、侯莫陳相、王軌各將一軍，分道出師；楊堅以隨國公從軍，攻城略地，戰後進封；獨孤永守洛陽，李穆經略長城，韋孝寬則經營晉北，攻取懷朔諸城，斷齊之西北屏障。北齊：高緯五七一年即位，人稱幼主，昏聵而多忌，和士開、祖珽把持朝政；斛律光封趙國公，鎮河朔，屢破周軍，是北齊軍力的柱石，卻因威名太重而屢遭猜忌，詔令交出兵柄、又以私傳軍令構陷，並追查其妻歐陽氏遣使請卜築城之事；高長恭同樣被剝奪兵權入京，懼禍及身而稱疾不出。段韶曾主張據河阻隔、棄平陽而固守，齊主不聽，這一失著在五年後被追驗。北齊末年的其他人物同樣在結局中現身：大將軍尉長命在青州追及齊後主，幽州刺史劉濟拒不降順而在齊亡之後北走突厥，高元海等人亦隨之。
peopleEn: The Northern Zhou: Yuwen Yong, the Emperor Wu of the Zhou, came to the throne as a child when Gao Zhan died in 571 and ruled until his own death in 578. His decisive act was killing the great chancellor Yuwen Hu in the palace in the tenth month of 572 and ruling personally, gathering the military command into the central command, and then leading the armies east himself in the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiande, determined to destroy Qi. Yuwen Xian, enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, was the marshal of the several armies and directed the operations along Pingyang and the Fen River; Yuwen Xin, Yuwen Sheng, Xin Shu, Doulu Xun, Houmochen Xiang and Wang Gui each led a separate column along a different route; Yang Jian, then Duke of Sui, served in the army, took part in the sieges and was enfeoffed in reward afterwards; Dugu Yong held Luoyang, Li Mu worked on the Great Wall line, and Wei Xiaokuan operated in northern Shanxi, seizing Huizhuo and other towns and cutting away the north-western shield of Qi. The Northern Qi: Gao Wei took the throne in 571 as a boy and was known as the Young Lord; he was dull-witted and jealous, and He Shikai and Zu Ting held the government. Hulü Guang, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, commanded the northern frontier, defeated the Zhou repeatedly and was the pillar of Qi's military strength, yet precisely because his fame was so great he was repeatedly suspected: edicts stripped him of his troops, a charge of privately transmitting orders was raised against him, and an inquiry was opened into a message carried by his wife Ouyang asking divination and the building of a city. Gao Changgong was likewise stripped of command and summoned to the capital, and from fear of the charges against him pretended illness and would not come out. Duan Shao had argued that the army should hold the river, abandon Pingyang and stand firm; the Qi ruler would not take his advice, and that misjudgement was vindicated five years later. Other figures of the closing years show up in the ending itself: the great general Yu Zhangming caught up with the Qi ruler at Qingzhou, and the governor of Youzhou, Liu Ji, refused to surrender and fled north to the Turks after Qi's fall, with Gao Yuanhai and others going with him.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬短劍是公元前一世紀的羅馬制式佩劍，短而重心靠前，設計出發點是刺而不是砍，銘文說的是「刺劍不是用來揮砍的，短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏」。然則五七二年的中原戰場上從未出現過這件兵器：中原兵卒手上是環首直刃刀、長柄矛、槊與戟，重騎靠槊衝陣，步卒以甲胄抵禦流矢而少持盾，格鬥的重心落在馬上的衝鋒而非面對面的短兵。雙方真正大量使用的裝備分三類：投射火器以弓、弩為主；步軍用矛槊配環首刀；重裝騎兵以鎧甲連馬鎧護身、以長槊衝鋒。攻城靠撞車、雲梯與以火燒木門的火箭，守城用弩機、擂石、滾木，史料有齊軍列陣以大排盾（彭排）蔽弩的記載。把羅馬短劍放回它自己的時空：公元前一世紀末的羅馬正處在共和末期軍制改革與帝國奠基的節點，標準步兵以短劍配大盾列成密集盾牆，刺擊的節奏與盾緣的掩護互相咬合；而同一時候的漢朝正當西漢，東西兩端隔地中海與絲路對望，漢使甘英西行至安息邊界而未能抵達大秦。兩套體系都靠「短兵相接」解決問題，解決方式卻截然不同：羅馬靠盾牆與刺突節奏，中原靠騎兵衝鋒與弓弩投射，前者重防禦縱深，後者重速度與衝量。羅馬短劍所代表的那條技術路徑，在五七二年的中原並沒有落腳的土壤。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card, the Roman gladius, was the standard sword of the Roman army in the first century before the common era: short, with its weight carried forward, and designed from the start to thrust rather than to slash. Its own inscription says it all: the stabbing sword was not meant to be swung, and in close fighting what mattered was the edge of the shield and the rhythm of the thrust. Yet this weapon never appeared on a battlefield in the Central Plains in 572. What the troops there actually carried were ring-pommel straight swords of the Han pattern, long spears, the long lance and the halberd. Armoured horse rode with the lance, while the infantry relied on armour to keep off arrows and rarely carried shields at all; the weight of hand-to-hand fighting fell on the charge from horseback rather than on duelling on foot. The equipment the two sides really used in bulk fell into three kinds: missiles, above all the bow and the crossbow; infantry spears and lances paired with ring-pommel swords; and heavy cavalry protected by armour and horse armour, charging with the long lance. Siege work relied on rams, scaling towers and fire arrows used to burn timber gates, while defence used mounted crossbows, stones rolled down the walls and logs dropped on attackers; the records also note Qi formations sheltering the crossbows behind large rows of shields. Set the gladius back in its own time: in the last century before the common era Rome stood at the hinge between the military reforms of the late Republic and the founding of the empire, and the standard infantryman carried the gladius and the large shield in a dense wall of shields, the rhythm of the thrust interlocking with the cover of the shield rim. At the same moment the Han dynasty in the east was in the middle of the Western Han, and the two ends of the world faced each other across the Mediterranean and the silk road; the Han envoy Gan Ying pushed westward as far as the frontier of Parthia and never reached Daqin. Both systems solved the problem of close combat, but in wholly different ways: Rome with the wall of shields and the rhythm of the thrust, the Central Plains with the cavalry charge and with missiles from bow and crossbow. The first built depth in defence, the second built speed and momentum. The technical path represented by the Roman gladius simply had no soil to take root in the Central Plains of 572.
tactics: 北周採大舉壓倒與沿河消耗兩手並用。建德元年冬，北周先發兵二十萬眾圍平陽（今山西臨汾），以平陽為橋頭堡，循汾水東下；此後數年反覆爭奪平陽、宜陽兩處要點，把戰爭拖成沿河的拉鋸。齊軍以斛律光為核心，據平陽、守河陰，寸土必爭；建德二年北周攻宜陽，斛律光率精騎大破周軍，段韶另以偏師擊破周軍另一部，齊人才穩住陣腳。建德四年十月，宇文邕自將二十餘萬眾濟河，志在直取平陽，斛律光集兵五萬騎拒於汾水，築壘扼守要津，北周軍久攻不克，糧道漸窘，軍中以夜渡強攻才把壘線打崩，齊軍全線潰散；斛律光馳回鄴城報敗，途中被追兵射中（一說為部下所殺），齊軍失去主帥與精騎，士氣崩解，而齊主仍不聽勸，繼續留戍。建德五年正月，北周長驅直抵鄴城，列營城外，撞車臨門、火攻門樓，齊後主授位幼子、自稱太上皇，與后妃幼主夜走青州；北周騎兵緊追不捨，大將軍尉長命於青州追及，齊後主被擒，鄴城遂陷，府庫、圖籍與河北諸州郡盡入北周之手。惟幽州一帶仍不肯歸順，齊幽州刺史劉濟與眾北走突厥，河北並非全數平定。
tacticsEn: The Zhou combined a mass blow with a war of attrition along the river. In the winter of the first year of Jiande it sent some two hundred thousand men to surround Pingyang, in present-day Linfen in Shanxi, using Pingyang as a bridgehead and pressing down the Fen River; for the next several years the two sides fought repeatedly over Pingyang and Yiyang, and the war degenerated into a grinding contest along the water. Qi's army was built around Hulü Guang, holding Pingyang and guarding Heyin, and contested every yard of ground; in the second year of Jiande the Zhou attacked Yiyang, Hulü Guang broke the Zhou main force with his cavalry and Duan Shao destroyed another column with a detachment of his own, and only then did Qi steady itself. In the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiande Yuwen Yong led more than two hundred thousand men across the river, resolved to take Pingyang directly. Hulü Guang gathered about fifty thousand cavalry to meet him on the Fen River, threw up a fortified camp to hold the crossing, and the Zhou army could not take it by assault; their supply line lengthened and their provisions ran short, and only a night crossing carried by picked troops broke the line of the camp and scattered the whole Qi army. Hulü Guang rode back to Ye to report the defeat and was shot by the pursuers on the way (some accounts say he was killed by his own men); Qi lost both its commander and its mounted elite, and its morale collapsed, while the Qi ruler still refused advice and left his troops in place. In the first month of the fifth year of Jiande the Zhou drove straight to Ye, camped outside the walls, brought rams against the gates and put fire to the gate towers. The Qi ruler handed the throne to his youngest son, styled himself the retired emperor, and fled by night with his empress, his concubines and the child heir to Qingzhou; the Zhou cavalry followed hard, the great general Yu Zhangming overtook him at Qingzhou, the Qi ruler was taken prisoner, and Ye fell. Its treasuries, its registers and the commanderies of Hebei passed into the hands of the Zhou. Youzhou alone refused to submit: the governor of Youzhou, Liu Ji, and his men went north to the Turks, and Hebei was not wholly pacified.
data: 時間：自建德元年（572）冬北周出兵圍平陽起，至建德五年（577）正月鄴城陷落，前後近五年；齊後主被擒在同年，誅之在建德五年十一月。兵力：建德四年十月宇文邕親征，號令諸軍二十餘萬，自關中、洛陽分道出師；斛律光在汾水一線集兵約五萬騎，齊軍精騎多集中於此人麾下。建德二年宜陽之戰，北周亦以二十萬眾來攻而被齊軍大破，士卒折損以萬計。城防與攻城：鄴城為北方第一大城，垣牆樓櫃皆經歷年增修，齊主徵京畿宿衛與城內丁壯守城，周軍則以撞車、火攻與雲梯攻城，並穴地填壕逼近牆根。戶口與物資：北齊天保以後戰亂不息，州郡戶口銳減；周軍克鄴之後括編河北州郡戶口，府兵編制自關中推廣到並、冀、兗、豫諸州，河北自此成為北周的兵源與糧源，《隋書·食貨志》所記北朝戶口以數百萬為量級、其後歷次括戶而漸增的趨勢，河北州郡的歸入正是其中最大的一次增補。人物年壽：斛律光以六十餘歲之齡戰歿於汾水，齊中最精銳的一支騎兵就此散盡。
dataEn: Timing: the war opened in the winter of the first year of Jiande, 572, when the Zhou sent troops to surround Pingyang, and it ended with the fall of Ye in the first month of the fifth year of Jiande, 577, a span of close to five years. The Qi ruler was taken prisoner in that same year and was put to death in the eleventh month of the fifth year of Jiande. Numbers: in the tenth month of the fourth year of Jiande Yuwen Yong led the campaign in person and called on more than two hundred thousand men of the several armies, moving out in separate columns from Guanzhong and from Luoyang; on the Fen River Hulü Guang concentrated about fifty thousand cavalry, and the finest of Qi's mounted troops were gathered under his command alone. In the battle of Yiyang in the second year of Jiande the Zhou also came with two hundred thousand men and was badly beaten, losing soldiers by the thousands. Fortification and siege: Ye was the first great city of the north, its ramparts and towers had been repaired and raised over many years, the Qi ruler called in the capital garrison and the able-bodied men of the city to man the walls, while the Zhou brought up rams, fire and scaling towers and dug in under the walls to fill the ditches. Population and supplies: after the Tianbao era of Northern Qi the wars never ceased and the registered households of the commanderies dwindled; after the Zhou took Ye they enrolled the households of the Hebei commanderies, and the fubing system was carried out of Guanzhong into the provinces of Bing, Ji, Yan and Yu, so that from then on Hebei became the source of men and grain for the Zhou. The figures of several hundred thousand households recorded for the northern dynasties in the Treatise on Economics of the Book of Sui, and the slow rise that followed as households were re-enrolled, had their largest single increment in the accession of the Hebei commanderies. Ages: Hulü Guang was past sixty when he fell on the Fen River, and with him the finest body of cavalry in Qi was scattered for good.
cause: 北周方面的推力來自三件事。其一，五七二年十月宇文邕在宮中殺死大冢宰宇文護，收回被相府把持的兵權，此後整軍經武、大興屯田、廣蓄馬匹，關中軍力由衰轉盛；其二，北周主動與北突厥修好，解除背後的牽制，東面又同陳朝保持和好，避免兩面作戰；其三，自西魏以來關隴集團的人脈與關中糧秣，使北周有能力支撐一場跨越河洛的大舉進攻。北齊方面的推力則來自內部的失序。乳母婁太后與幼主高緯寵信和士開、祖珽，斛律光因威名太重屢被詆毀，幾遭解去兵柄，高長恭同樣被削權入京、稱疾避禍，宿將離心，朝廷便拿不住北齊最能打的兩支力量；段韶曾建議放棄平陽、據河而守，齊主猶豫不決，一再把可以集中的兵力拆散使用。而外部的結構變化同樣重要：柔然控弦漠北，一旦北齊在河洛敗績，柔然便再無牽制北周之力，北周的突厥盟友則可放手。建德元年冬北周大軍圍平陽，等於給了北齊最後一次體面反擊的機會，卻也暴露了它已無力再守住河東與河北的門戶，戰爭就此由試探轉為傾國之役。
causeEn: The push on the Zhou side came from three things. First, in the tenth month of 572 Yuwen Yong killed the great chancellor Yuwen Hu inside the palace and took back the military authority that the chancellery had held; he then rebuilt the army, expanded the garrison farms and raised horses in numbers, and the military strength of Guanzhong turned from decline to growth. Second, the Zhou proactively made peace with the Northern Turks, removing the pressure from behind, and kept on good terms with the Chen dynasty in the east so as never to fight on two fronts. Third, the network of the Guanlong group that had grown out of the Western Wei, together with the grain of Guanzhong, allowed the Zhou to sustain a great offensive spanning the Yellow River and the Luo valley. The push on the Qi side came instead from internal disorder. The wet nurse Lou and the boy emperor Gao Wei favoured He Shikai and Zu Ting; Hulü Guang, because his fame was so great, was repeatedly slandered and came close to being stripped of his command; Gao Changgong was likewise shorn of his authority and summoned to the capital, pleading illness to stay out of harm's way. The veterans had lost their heart, and the court could no longer hold on to the two most formidable forces Qi possessed. Duan Shao had proposed abandoning Pingyang and standing on the river, and the Qi ruler hesitated, again and again dispersing troops that could have been concentrated. The change in the external structure mattered as much: the Rouran held the northern steppe, and once Qi was beaten in the Yellow River and Luo valley, the Rouran would have no strength left to contain the Zhou, whose Turkic allies would be free to act. The Zhou army's encirclement of Pingyang in the winter of the first year of Jiande gave Qi a last chance to strike back in respectable fashion, but it also exposed the fact that Qi no longer had the strength to hold the gateway to Hedong and Hebei. The war turned from probing into a war aimed at the destruction of a state.
impact: 此役的直接後果是南北一統的格局被打開一個缺口。河北州郡盡歸北周，府兵制自關中推廣到並、冀、兗、豫，北周的兵源、馬政與糧源為之一新；北齊的士族與官吏多仕北周，河北的漢族菁英自此進入關隴集團的邊緣。北周亦以此役為契機推行漢化與滅佛。建德三年（574）周武帝詔斷佛道二教，僧尼還俗，寺產入官，軍隊所至常以佛寺充作營房，史載沙門與將領曾為此力辯；戰爭的軍費開支正是這場宗教變革得以推行下去的背景。長遠看，此役奠定的是隋的天下。五七七年之後北周據有河北，關隴集團在北方一家獨大，四年之後楊堅代周建隋，五八九年隋滅陳，統一全國；隋唐兩代的府兵制、關隴軍團與長安的首都地位，源頭都在這幾年取得的河北人力與馬力。代價同樣明顯：連年大舉徵發使關中與河北疲敝，府兵之負擔加重，北周晚年的財政與兵源壓力一路累積到周宣帝朝，楊堅得以乘隙專政，五八一年受禪代周。五七二年的這場戰爭，最終變成了隋朝的鋪路石。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the war was a breach in the pattern of a north divided from a south divided. The commanderies of Hebei passed to the Zhou, the fubing system was carried out of Guanzhong into Bing, Ji, Yan and Yu, and the Zhou's supply of men, horses and grain was transformed by it. The scholars and officials of Qi mostly entered the service of the Zhou, and the Han elite of Hebei from then on stood at the fringe of the Guanlong group. The war also became the occasion for the Zhou to push ahead with its sinicisation and its suppression of Buddhism. In the third year of Jiande, 574, the Emperor Wu of Zhou issued an edict cutting the Buddhist and the Daoist faiths, returning monks and nuns to lay life and taking temple property into the treasury; troops on campaign commonly quartered in Buddhist monasteries, and the records show monks arguing with generals on the point. The cost of the war was itself the background that allowed that religious upheaval to be carried through. In the long run the war laid the foundations of the Sui. After 577 the Zhou held Hebei, the Guanlong group stood supreme in the north, four years later Yang Jian replaced the Zhou and founded the Sui, and in 589 the Sui destroyed the Chen and unified the empire. The fubing system of the Sui and Tang, the Guanlong military group, and the standing of Chang'an as a capital all trace back to the manpower and the remounts that Hebei gave up in these years. The cost was equally plain. Levies raised year after year exhausted Guanzhong and Hebei alike, the burden of the fubing grew heavier, and the fiscal and manpower pressure of the late Zhou accumulated all the way into the reign of the Emperor Xuan, giving Yang Jian his opening to take power; in 581 he received the abdication and replaced the Zhou. The war that began in 572 became in the end a stepping stone for the Sui.
result: 建德五年正月，北周軍入鄴城，北齊亡國。齊後主高緯自鄴出奔青州，途中被大將軍尉長命追及擒獲，送回鄴城；同年十一月，北周在鄴城將高緯與其弟高潤一併誅殺。齊幼主高煒在奔逃中脫走，輾轉至陳，陳朝授以官職，寄居江南；齊大將軍段韶見大勢已去，率眾降周；幽州刺史劉濟與高元海等仍據幽州不降，齊亡之後北走突厥，幽州一隅要等到隋朝才真正入中原。從戰爭全局看，斛律光的死在汾水比鄴城城破更具決定性：一支久經訓練的騎兵統帥被射殺於陣前，齊軍的精銳與指揮一併崩解，之後的崩潰便只是時間問題。北周由此統一長江以北，佔有河北的人力、物力與馬力，府兵與屯田因之壯大，關隴集團從一個關中的軍事聯盟變成統治半壁江山的政權。餘波延伸到下一代：北周統治北方不足十年便因宣帝朝政治昏亂而被隋取代，隋的開皇之治、隋唐一統的格局與長安作為都城，都可以在這一場歷時五年的滅國戰爭裡找到起點。北齊亡國之後，河北進入長達二十餘年的相對安定期，直到隋末唐初的戰亂再起。
resultEn: In the first month of the fifth year of Jiande the Zhou army entered Ye and the Northern Qi went out of existence. Gao Wei, the Qi ruler, fled from Ye toward Qingzhou, was overtaken and taken prisoner on the road by the great general of the army, Yu Zhangming, and was brought back to Ye; in the eleventh month of that same year the Zhou executed Gao Wei and his brother Gao Run at Ye. The child heir Gao Wei the younger escaped in the flight and made his way in stages to the Chen, which granted him an office and settled him in the south; the Qi great general Duan Shao, seeing that the situation was lost, came over to the Zhou with his men; the governor of Youzhou, Liu Ji, with Gao Yuanhai and others, still held Youzhou and would not surrender, and after the fall of Qi they went north to the Turks, so that Youzhou was not truly brought into the Central Plain until the Sui. Viewed as a whole, the death of Hulü Guang on the Fen River mattered more than the breach of Ye's walls: a commander of long-trained cavalry was shot down before the line, and the elite and the command of the Qi army collapsed together, after which the fall of the state was only a matter of time. The Zhou thereby unified everything north of the Yangtze, gained the men, the goods and the horses of Hebei, saw fubing and the garrison farms grow in strength, and turned the Guanlong group from a military league in Guanzhong into a government ruling half the empire. The aftershocks carried into the next generation: the Zhou ruled the north for less than ten years before the disorder of the reign of the Emperor Xuan let the Sui replace it, and the government of the Kaihuang era, the pattern of Sui-Tang unification and the standing of Chang'an as a capital can all be traced back to the beginning of this war of five years that destroyed a state. After the fall of Northern Qi, Hebei entered a relative peace lasting more than twenty years, until the wars of the late Sui and the early Tang began once more.
